question.problem:
The table below gives the values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p,$ where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. Find the value of $z$ such that $P(Z\le z)=0.015.$

| $\,p\,$ | $0.965$ | $0.970$ | $0.975$ | $0.980$ | $0.985$ | $0.990$ | $0.995$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,1.8119\,$ | $\,1.8808\,$ | $\,1.9600\,$ | $\,2.0537\,$ | $\,2.1701\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ | $\,2.5758\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
From the table, notice that

$$
P(Z\le 2.1701)=0.985.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
P(Z\ge 2.1701)=1-0.985=0.015.
$$

By the symmetry of the standard normal distribution, we have

$$
Φ(-2.1701)=0.015.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14165008/assets/47a123a730cf175bea1d1887ffdc5a9feb3e1d8f07208c28a9f893a9a1688005.png)

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-2.1701) & =0.015 \\ P(Z\le -2.1701) & =0.015.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required value of $z$ is $-2.1701.$
